cards.explanation: The answer is all their brothers plus the priests and Levites. That's the guest list, friends. David says to send word far and wide to “…the rest of our brothers in all the land of Israel, and also to the priests and Levites in their cities and pasturelands, so that they may join us.” He wants the whole nation in on this. Nobody gets left off this invite, and nobody has to hit "reply all."

The answer is ark. David says, “Then let us bring back the ark of our God…” The whole plan is about this one holy thing. Verse 6 calls it the ark of God the LORD, who is enthroned between the cherubim. Nothing about this plan is small.

The answer is that they did not inquire of God under Saul. Saul was Israel's king before David (1 Samuel 11:15; 2 Samuel 5:3), and David says, “…for we did not inquire of Him in the days of Saul.” David also asks the leaders if this is of the LORD their God (verse 2). I respect a man who checks first, because I've skipped the recipe before and learned that lesson with flour on my hat.

The answer is True. The text says, “And because this proposal seemed right to all the people, the whole assembly agreed to it.” A whole assembly on the same page is a beautiful thing. Even my cookie cutter kids couldn't agree on a topping.

The answer is on a new cart. Verse 7 says, “So they carried the ark of God from the house of Abinadab on a new cart…” Abinadab's house is where they pick the ark up. I know a thing or two about being replaced by something shinier, since a new stamper took my spot on the Millers' counter, so I notice a new cart.

The answer is False. The text says, “David and all the Israelites were celebrating before God with all their might, with songs and on harps and lyres, with tambourines, cymbals, and trumpets.” That's songs, strings and a full brass and percussion section. They're celebrating with all their might. Nobody on that road was using their inside voice.

The answer is that he takes hold of the ark, and this is where the story turns. The text says, “…Uzzah reached out and took hold of the ark, because the oxen had stumbled.” Uzzah is one of the two men guiding the cart. One moment David and all the Israelites are celebrating, and then Uzzah reaches out. I think this is the part where everybody holds their breath.

The answer is angry. The text says, “Then David became angry because the LORD had burst forth against Uzzah.” David even names the place Perez-uzzah. I think this one hurts, friends, because a celebration just turned into a loss. It's okay to say this is a heavy part.

The answer is David asking, “How can I ever bring the ark of God to me?” The text says that day David feared God and asked that question. The big plan he started with now has a big question on it. I think David is thinking hard about what just happened.

The answer is False. The text says, “So he did not move the ark with him to the City of David; instead, he took it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.” David's big plan hits a pause. The ark goes to a different house. The story isn't finished, though.

The answer is that the LORD blesses his household and all he owns. The text says, “Thus the ark of God remained with the family of Obed-edom in his house for three months, and the LORD blessed his household and everything he owned.” The blessing comes during those three months with the ark. I think a blessing like that is a sweet thing to read after such a heavy moment.
